text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"The IAEA reports nuclear is a low-carbon source producing about 10 percent of world electricity.","cited_pids":["7e88e103d8fb#0"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"Higher nuclear output helped level global CO2 emissions in 2019.","cited_pids":["7e88e103d8fb#0"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"Nuclear plants emit no greenhouse gases during operation.","cited_pids":["8ef6c9360938#3"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"Life-cycle emissions per unit of nuclear electricity are about the same as wind and one-third of solar.","cited_pids":["8ef6c9360938#3"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"In a study of 16 nuclear-generating countries, cutting CO2 by 1% required a 2.907% increase in nuclear generation versus 4.902% for renewables.","cited_pids":["946b45d61e84#0"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"An analysis of construction projects found nuclear plants average cost overruns of about 102.5%.","cited_pids":["06384d0fb532#2"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"Industry commentary notes nuclear cost overruns continue while renewable costs fall.","cited_pids":["a518156a3214#3"]},{"cid":"c8","text":"A Swedish model found little cost benefit in rebuilding nuclear once old plants close, given low-carbon alternatives.","cited_pids":["6b0ccdbcf9aa#1"]}]}
